- name: fct_trip_event
  description: |
    One row per recorded trip lifecycle event emitted from the start, pause, resume, and end raw event streams.
    This model supports event-level operational analysis and troubleshooting of how trips progress through their lifecycle.
    The time axis is `event_ts`, which represents when the source event occurred, and `event_date` is the calendar date derived from that event timestamp.
  columns:
  - name: event_key
    description: Stable key for a single trip event record. Each value should identify one event instance across the unified event stream.
    tests:
    - unique
    - not_null
  - name: trip_id
    description: Source trip identifier carried on the event. Multiple event records can share the same trip_id because a trip can have start, pause, resume, and end events.
    tests:
    - not_null
  - name: event_ts
    description: Timestamp when the trip event occurred in the source system. This is the primary timestamp for event sequencing and time-series analysis.
    tests:
    - not_null
  - name: event_date
    description: Calendar date derived from `event_ts`. Use this for daily rollups of event activity rather than as a trip completion date.
    tests:
    - not_null
  - name: event_name
    description: Normalized business event name describing the lifecycle step, such as trip start or trip end.
  - name: source_event_model
    description: Name of the upstream event model that produced the record. Useful for lineage and debugging source-specific behavior.
  - name: rider_id
    description: Rider identifier present on the event, when available.
  - name: bike_id
    description: Bike identifier present on the event, when available.
  - name: event_payload_present_flag
    description: Indicates whether the underlying source event included a payload. This helps distinguish missing event content from valid events with sparse attributes.
  - name: event_type_raw
    description: Raw event type value from the source feed before normalization.
  - name: message_type
    description: Latest source message classification carried on the event record.
  - name: isbn
    description: Source ISBN-like identifier associated with the bike message payload. Its business meaning depends on upstream device messaging conventions.
- name: fct_trip
  description: |
    One row per trip_id representing the assembled trip lifecycle across its underlying events.
    This model supports decisions about trip completion, trip quality, and rider or bike usage by summarizing each trip into business-ready metrics.
    The primary time axes are `trip_start_ts` and `trip_end_ts`, while `trip_activity_date` is the activity date assigned to the trip for daily reporting.
  columns:
  - name: trip_key
    description: Stable key for the trip fact row. Each value should identify one trip-level record.
    tests:
    - unique
    - not_null
  - name: trip_id
    description: Source trip identifier used to assemble events into a trip. This should be present for every fact row.
    tests:
    - not_null
  - name: rider_id
    description: Rider associated with the trip. Use with care if upstream events can be incomplete or malformed.
    tests:
    - relationships:
        to: ref('dim_rider')
        field: rider_id
  - name: bike_id
    description: Bike used for the trip. This links the trip to bike-level lifecycle and utilization analysis.
    tests:
    - relationships:
        to: ref('dim_bike')
        field: bike_id
  - name: trip_start_ts
    description: Timestamp of the anchored trip start event. Null or unexpected values can indicate incomplete event capture.
  - name: trip_end_ts
    description: Timestamp of the anchored trip end event. Trips still in progress may not have a populated end timestamp.
  - name: trip_activity_date
    description: Reporting date assigned to the trip for daily analysis. This is the business date to use in aggregates, not necessarily the same as the end date in every edge case.
    tests:
    - not_null
  - name: trip_status
    description: Business status of the trip, such as completed or in progress, based on the available event pattern.
  - name: trip_duration_seconds
    description: Duration of the trip in seconds, typically measured from anchored start to anchored end. In-progress or low-quality trips may have null, zero, or non-final values.
  - name: total_event_count
    description: Count of all lifecycle events attached to the trip. Higher counts can reflect pauses and resumes, not necessarily duplicate trips.
  - name: pause_event_count
    description: Number of pause events observed for the trip.
  - name: resume_event_count
    description: Number of resume events observed for the trip.
  - name: data_quality_flag
    description: Indicator that the assembled trip has a known data quality concern, such as missing anchors or inconsistent event patterns.
  - name: trip_grain_type
    description: Label describing the trip record grain or assembly logic used to produce the row.
  - name: anchor_start_event_key
    description: Event key chosen as the canonical trip start anchor.
  - name: anchor_end_event_key
    description: Event key chosen as the canonical trip end anchor.
- name: dim_bike
  description: |
    One row per bike_id describing the observed bike entity across trip events.
    This model supports decisions about fleet coverage, bike recency, and bike-level reporting joins from trip facts.
    The time axes `first_seen_ts` and `last_seen_ts` represent the earliest and latest event timestamps where the bike was observed, and the date columns are their calendar-date counterparts.
  columns:
  - name: bike_key
    description: Stable surrogate key for the bike dimension row.
    tests:
    - unique
    - not_null
  - name: bike_id
    description: Natural bike identifier observed in trip events. This is the primary business key for joining bike usage.
    tests:
    - unique
    - not_null
  - name: first_seen_ts
    description: Earliest event timestamp at which the bike was seen in the trip event stream.
  - name: last_seen_ts
    description: Most recent event timestamp at which the bike was seen in the trip event stream.
  - name: first_seen_date
    description: Calendar date of the bike's first observed event.
  - name: last_seen_date
    description: Calendar date of the bike's most recent observed event.
  - name: latest_message_type
    description: Most recent source message type observed for the bike. This reflects the latest known message, not a long-term classification.
  - name: latest_isbn
    description: Most recent ISBN-like identifier observed for the bike from event payloads. Because it is taken from the latest event, historical values may differ.
- name: dim_rider
  description: |
    One row per rider_id describing the observed rider entity across trip events.
    This model supports rider-level segmentation, recency analysis, and consistent joins from trip facts and rider aggregates.
    The time axes `first_seen_ts` and `last_seen_ts` represent the earliest and latest event timestamps where the rider was observed, and the date columns are their calendar-date counterparts.
  columns:
  - name: rider_key
    description: Stable surrogate key for the rider dimension row.
    tests:
    - unique
    - not_null
  - name: rider_id
    description: Natural rider identifier observed in trip events. This is the primary business key for rider-level joins.
    tests:
    - unique
    - not_null
  - name: first_seen_ts
    description: Earliest event timestamp at which the rider was seen in the trip event stream.
  - name: last_seen_ts
    description: Most recent event timestamp at which the rider was seen in the trip event stream.
  - name: first_seen_date
    description: Calendar date of the rider's first observed event.
  - name: last_seen_date
    description: Calendar date of the rider's most recent observed event.
- name: agg_rider_daily_trip_activity
  description: |
    One row per rider_id and activity_date summarizing that rider's trip activity for the day.
    This model supports daily rider engagement, anomaly monitoring, and operational reporting on completed versus in-progress trip behavior.
    The time axis is `activity_date`, which represents the reporting date assigned from trip activity rather than a rider signup or profile date.
  columns:
  - name: rider_id
    description: Rider whose trip activity is being summarized for the day.
    tests:
    - not_null
    - relationships:
        to: ref('dim_rider')
        field: rider_id
  - name: activity_date
    description: Reporting date for the rider's aggregated trip activity.
    tests:
    - not_null
  - name: trip_count
    description: Total number of trip fact rows attributed to the rider on the activity date. This can include trips in multiple statuses.
  - name: completed_trip_count
    description: Number of trips on the activity date that were classified as completed.
  - name: in_progress_trip_count
    description: Number of trips on the activity date that remained in progress at reporting time.
  - name: anomaly_trip_count
    description: Number of trips flagged as anomalous or low quality for the rider on the activity date. Interpret alongside data quality rules in the upstream trip fact.
  - name: distinct_bike_count
    description: Count of distinct bikes used by the rider on the activity date.
  - name: total_trip_duration_seconds
    description: Sum of trip duration seconds across the rider's trips for the activity date. Incomplete trips can reduce comparability across days.
  - name: avg_trip_duration_seconds
    description: Average trip duration seconds across the rider's trips for the activity date. This average may be skewed by incomplete or anomalous trips if they are included upstream.

`models/schema.yml` documents all six mart models with column-level descriptions and includes key tests such as `unique`, `not_null`, and `relationships` between facts/aggregates and the rider and bike dimensions.
The documented business domain is trip lifecycle analytics, with event-level, trip-level, rider-level, bike-level, and daily activity/utilization reporting grains represented in the marts layer.

findings: models/marts/fct_trip_event.sql excludes every source row where `trip IS NOT NULL` is false in all four branch CTEs (`trip_end_events`, `trip_pause_events`, `trip_resume_events`, `trip_start_events`). The approved spec for `fct_trip_event` allows `trip_id` to be null and `fct_trip` explicitly depends on those null-`trip_id` events for `start_anchored` and `orphan_end` trip construction, so this will undercount events and make fallback trip/session decisions impossible. Smallest next action: remove the `trip IS NOT NULL` filters while still retaining the `event_at IS NOT NULL` timestamp filter.

models/marts/fct_trip.sql does not conform to the required trip-construction contract: it only builds grouped `trip_id` rows (`trip_rollup GROUP BY trip_id`) and hard-codes `trip_grain_type` as `'trip_id'`, with no visible `start_anchored` or `orphan_end` path. In the same file, event logic keys off `event_name = 'trip_start'/'trip_end'/'trip_pause'/'trip_resume'`, but the `fct_trip_event` spec defines canonical `event_name` values as exactly `start`, `end`, `pause`, and `resume`. This will produce incorrect trip rows, pause/resume counts, and status assignment relative to the approved model semantics. Smallest next action: implement the three required construction paths and align all `event_name` predicates and `trip_grain_type` values to the spec.

models/marts/agg_rider_daily_trip_activity.sql aggregates all `fct_trip` rows after only filtering `rider_id IS NOT NULL` and `trip_activity_date IS NOT NULL`; the business KPI fields `trip_count` (`COUNT(*)`), `distinct_bike_count` (`COUNT(DISTINCT bike_id)`), `total_trip_duration_seconds` (`SUM(trip_duration_seconds)`), and `avg_trip_duration_seconds` (`AVG(trip_duration_seconds)`) are not restricted to `trip_status IN ('completed','in_progress')` as required by the spec. This will mix anomalous trips into rider-day KPI reporting. Smallest next action: apply the `trip_status IN ('completed','in_progress')` condition to the business metrics and leave `anomaly_trip_count` as the only non-business-status count.

models/marts/agg_bike_daily_utilization.sql computes several core business KPIs over all rows in `bike_trips`, not just `trip_status in ('completed','in_progress')` as required by the spec: `COUNT(*) AS trip_count`, `COUNT(DISTINCT rider_id) AS distinct_rider_count`, `SUM(trip_duration_seconds) AS total_trip_duration_seconds`, and `AVG(trip_duration_seconds) AS avg_trip_duration_seconds` have no status filter. This will overstate daily bike utilization whenever anomalous/non-business statuses exist. Smallest next action: make these aggregates conditional on `trip_status in ('completed','in_progress')` (or filter the input rows for those metrics only).

models/marts/agg_bike_daily_utilization.sql defines `anomaly_trip_count` as `COUNT_IF(data_quality_flag <> 'ok')`, but the approved spec defines this metric as count of rows where `trip_status not in ('completed','in_progress')`. These are not equivalent business rules, so anomaly counts can disagree with the contract and mislead monitoring decisions. Smallest next action: derive `anomaly_trip_count` from `trip_status`, not `data_quality_flag`.

models/marts/agg_bike_daily_utilization.sql uses `SUM(trip_duration_seconds) AS total_trip_duration_seconds` without `COALESCE`, while the spec explicitly requires null `trip_duration_seconds` values to contribute 0 and declares the output non-null. If a bike/day group has only null durations, `SUM(...)` will return null instead of 0, producing incorrect totals. Smallest next action: coalesce the summed duration to 0 in the final select.
